fact: Falcon Point at Saddleback's Design Standards, adopted by its Design Review Committee on June 27, 2022, mention artificial turf only to keep it and any other floor covering off the front porch, patios and balconies, and they do not permit balconies at all.
quote: ARTIFICIAL TURF – Neither artificial turf nor any other floor covering shall be used on the front porch, patio, or any balcony. … BALCONIES - Not permitted. … THESE DESIGN STANDARDS WERE ADOPTED BY THE DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE on the 27th day of June 2022.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Sections II.H and II.J, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Read from CDFPS.GOV.xx.DesignGuidelinesUpdatedJune2022.pdf, linked from the documents page (the file links are signed and expire, so the page is the source). Artificial turf appears nowhere else in the standards or the declaration.

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards require Design Review Committee approval for landscaping and for any improvement they do not list, and require landscaping to follow all of the Town of Firestone's requirements.
quote: Proposed Improvements, which are not specifically listed in this Section II. of the Design Standards require Committee approval. … LANDSCAPE AND MAINTENANCE - Committee approval is required. … Landscaping shall follow all requirements of the Town of Firestone.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Sections II.A and II.PP, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Putting greens and artificial turf in the yard are not listed items of their own, so II.A.3 and II.PP both send them to the committee.

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards say Town of Firestone approvals and permits must still be obtained where required, and that committee approval is no assurance a project meets government rules or needs no permit.
quote: Approval and permits from the Town of Firestone shall be obtained where required. Approval by the Committee will not constitute assurance that Existing Improvements or Proposed Improvements comply with applicable governmental requirements and regulations, or that a permit or approvals are not also required from applicable governmental bodies.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section I.F, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards have the committee judge new work by whether it harmonizes with the existing surroundings, residences and landscaping, and require an improvement's style to match the homes and lots in the same general area of the community.
quote: To interpret these Design Standards by exercising its reasonable judgment to achieve the end that all Proposed Improvements conform to and harmonize with the existing surroundings, residences, landscaping, and structures. … The architectural style of a Proposed Improvement shall be consistent with the style and character of the Homes and Lots built in the same general area of the Community. The Committee in its sole discretion shall determine such consistency.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Sections I.C and II.A, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's declaration, in the landscaping section that has each owner landscape a lot within 180 days of acquiring it (or by the following October 1), requires landscaping plans to be professionally done, to follow the design guidelines and to be approved by the Design Review Committee before the landscaping goes in.
quote: The Owner of each Lot (other than Declarant or a Builder) shall install landscaping on such Lot within one hundred eighty (180) days after acquisition of such Lot by such Owner if said acquisition occurs between April 1 and October 1 … Landscaping plans and other required documents shall be professionally done, shall be in accordance with the design guidelines, and shall be submitted to the Design Review Committee for review and approval prior to the installation of landscaping, except where installed by the Declarant.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 10.13 (recorded September 20, 2019, Weld County Reception No. 4525105), on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Read from CDFPS.GOV.xx.20190920.DeclarationofCovenantsConditionsandRestrictions.pdf, re-downloaded from the documents page 2026-09-26 (same file, md5 30e0848d…). The sentence sits in the owner's first-landscaping clause; the Design Standards (III.D) ask for professional plans only for major improvements and say simple drawings may be sufficient for others, so the page reports the difference and sends owners to the committee. The First Amendment (recorded July 28, 2020) changes only the working-capital contribution.

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards ask for a signed request form and complete drawings, drawn to scale and preferably from a lot survey, showing the lot lines, the house, existing improvements and the proposed work with its materials and colors.
quote: All Design Review Requests should be made to the Association's Management Company and must include the following: … One (1) copy of the "Design Review Request" form, attached to these Design Standards as Attachment 2, which must be signed and dated by the Owner; and … One (1) copy of complete drawings, specifications, and plans … The drawing, specification, or plan should be done to scale, and should depict the property lines of the Lot and the outside boundary lines of the Home as located on the Lot. Drawings made from a Lot survey base are preferred; … Existing Improvements, in addition to the Home, should be shown on the drawing, specification, or plan, and identified or labeled. … there should be a brief description of the Proposed Improvement, including the materials to be used and the colors.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Sections III.C and III.D, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards recommend telling neighbors about a project before submitting it, and let the committee ask adjacent neighbors for input.
quote: It is suggested and recommended that Owners advise neighbors of their Proposed Improvements prior to making a Design Review Request to the Committee. The Committee, in its discretion, may request adjacent neighbor input as part of its deliberation process.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section III.B, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: No fee is due when a Falcon Point design request is submitted, but the committee's review costs, reasonable engineering consultant fees included, are charged to the owner and payable before final approval.
quote: No fee is charged at the time the Design Review Request is submitted for review by the Committee. All costs for review of Design Review Requests shall be borne by the submitting Owner, shall be assessed to the submitting Owner, and shall be payable prior to final approval. Potential costs for review of Design Review Requests may include any reasonable engineering consultant fees or other fees incurred by the Committee in its review.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section III.E, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Declaration Section 5.2.3 says the same: the committee may require reimbursement of its actual review expenses, levied against the lot.

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards require approved work to follow the approved plans and to be finished within one year of the committee's approval.
quote: After approval of any Proposed Improvement by the Committee, the Proposed Improvement should be accomplished as promptly and diligently as possible and in complete conformity with the approved plans, drawings, and descriptions as well as any other terms and conditions of the approval. The work must be completed, in any event, within one (1) year after approval by the Committee.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section III.G, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Declaration Section 5.6 sets the same one-year limit and lets the committee grant extensions in its discretion.

fact: Falcon Point's declaration gives the Design Review Committee 45 days after a complete submission to decide a request, and a request it has not decided by then is deemed denied.
quote: The Design Review Committee shall decide each request for approval within forty-five (45) days after the complete submission of all plans, specifications and other materials and information which the Committee may require in conjunction therewith. If the Design Review Committee fails to decide any request within forty-five (45) days after the complete submission of all plans, specifications, materials and other information with respect thereto, then such request shall be deemed to have been denied by the Committee.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 5.4 (recorded September 20, 2019), on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Design Standards III.F repeats the 45 days and adds that all committee decisions will be in writing.

fact: The association's FAQ, last updated September 17, 2025, says architectural requests go in through TownSq, are reviewed by the Board of Directors and may take up to 30 days for a response, and names Goodwin & Company as the manager.
quote: Last Update: 9/17/2025 … All requests must be submitted via TownSq. … Once the application is submitted it will be reviewed by the Board of Directors. A response may take up to 30 days from the date of submission. … Management Goodwin & Company
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback HOA, Frequently Asked Questions page (TownSq), last updated September 17, 2025
notes: Re-fetched 2026-09-26. The FAQ's reviewer (the board) and clock (30 days) differ from the declaration (the Design Review Committee, 45 days, silence = denial). The page says so and sends owners to the manager.

fact: Falcon Point's declaration covers 80 lots, Lots 1 to 34 of Block 1, 1 to 21 of Block 2 and 1 to 25 of Block 3 of the Saddleback Filing No. 3 Final Plat recorded October 22, 2018, and allows at most 85 lots in all.
quote: "Lots that May Be Included" means (85) Lots, which shall be the maximum number of Lots that may be subject to this Declaration … the final plat of Saddleback Filing No. 3 Final Plat, recorded on October 22, 2018, at Reception No. 4440395 in the records of the office of the Clerk and Recorder of Weld County, Colorado … Lots 1 through 34, Block 1 Lots 1 through 21, Block 2 Lots 1 through 25, Block 3
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 1.19 and Exhibit A (recorded September 20, 2019), on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: In Colorado's statewide parcel layer, 58 of the 80 lots in Saddleback Filing No. 3 measure between 0.14 and 0.17 acre (about 6,100 to 7,400 square feet), with the smallest at 0.136 acre and the largest at 0.269 acre.
quote: legalDesc: Lot 9 Block 1 SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3 | landAcres: 0.1358625 … legalDesc: Lot 12 Block 2 SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3 | landAcres: 0.2690932
source_label: State of Colorado, Colorado Public Parcels (composite of county parcel data), Weld County parcels with subdivision name SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3, queried 2026-09-26
notes: Queried the layer's REST query endpoint (where countyName='Weld' AND subName LIKE 'SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3%'): 90 parcels, 80 of them Lots 1-34 Block 1, 1-21 Block 2 and 1-25 Block 3, plus 10 tracts. landAcres: 58 lots at 0.14 to under 0.17, 4 under 0.14, 18 at 0.17 or more (13 at 0.2 or more); median 0.152. Acreage is the whole lot, house included. Square feet = acres x 43,560, rounded to the nearest hundred. Owner, value and sale fields were not requested. Re-queried 2026-09-26 with the same result (90 parcels, 80 lots, 58 in 0.14 to under 0.17 acre, min Lot 9 Block 1, max Lot 12 Block 2).

fact: In Colorado's statewide parcel layer, Tracts D and F of Saddleback Filing No. 3 share a boundary with the 253-acre parcel that Weld County's legal description calls Saddleback Golf Course, and none of the filing's 80 house lots touches that parcel; the nearest, Lot 11 of Block 1, is about 14 meters away.
quote: KNOWN AS SADDLEBACK GOLF COURSE | landAcres: 253.10506702 … Tract D SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3 … Tract F SADDLEBACK FG NO. 3
source_label: State of Colorado, Colorado Public Parcels (composite of county parcel data), Weld County parcels for Saddleback Filing No. 3 and the Saddleback Golf Course parcel, queried 2026-09-26
notes: Re-queried 2026-09-26 (outSR 4326) and measured lot and tract vertices against the 253-acre parcel's edges: Tracts D and F at 0 m, Tract C about 3 m, Tract E about 13 m, Lot 11 Block 1 about 14 m, Lot 20 Block 1 about 21 m. What lies between each lot and the course (street, tract, trail) was not checked. Tracts D and F are not among the HOA's common elements (Exhibit B lists Tracts A, B1, B2 and G). The builder's sales pages were not read and are not cited.

fact: Falcon Point's declaration reserves drainage easements across the rear 5 feet and side 5 feet of every lot and bars improvements or grading changes there that would redirect, block or slow water moving through the swales.
quote: Declarant hereby reserves, to itself and to the Association, easements for drainage and drainage facilities across the five (5) rear and five (5) side feet of each Lot; … Except for residences as provided in the preceding sentence, no Improvements shall be placed or permitted to remain on any Lot nor shall any change in grading be permitted to exist which may change the direction of flow or obstruct or retard the flow of water or other moisture through channels or swales within such rear and side yard drainage easements.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 9.5 (recorded September 20, 2019), on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: The declaration's definition of Improvements (Section 1) includes landscaping, sod and gravel.

fact: Falcon Point's declaration bars owners from obstructing a lot's established drainage and requires a plan approved by the Design Review Committee before that drainage is changed.
quote: Each Owner and the Association agree, for themselves and their heirs, personal representatives, successors and assigns, that they will not in any way interfere with or obstruct the established drainage pattern over any real property. Except as to the Declarant or a Builder, in the event that it is necessary or desirable to change the established drainage over any Lot or Common Elements, then the party responsible for the maintenance of such real property shall submit a plan to the Design Review Committee for its review and approval
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 8.4 (recorded September 20, 2019), on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards require a xeriscape to combine rock, mulches, shrubs, trees, grasses and ground covers, with plants covering at least 65% of the area to be landscaped at maturity.
quote: Xeriscape landscapes must include a combination of rock, mulches, shrubs, trees, grasses, and ground covers. A minimum of sixty-five percent (65%) of the area to be landscaped must be covered by plant material at maturity.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.QQQQ, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: The standards do not say whether artificial turf is part of 'the area to be landscaped' for this rule.

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards require committee approval for a hot tub, which must sit in the rear yard as an integral part of the deck or patio and the rear-yard landscaping, and do not permit tennis courts.
quote: HOT TUBS - Committee approval is required. Design must include the hot tub as an integral part of the deck or patio area and of the rear yard landscaping. Hot tub must be in the rear yard. … TENNIS COURTS - Not permitted.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Sections II.JJ and II.CCCC, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards require committee approval for play and sports equipment, which goes in the rear or side yard, should not exceed 14 feet in height, and may need written consent from adjacent neighbors.
quote: PLAY AND SPORTS EQUIPMENT - Committee approval is required. Equipment shall be located in the rear or side yard. Size of play yards will be considered on a case-by-case basis depending on Lot size and proximity to neighbors. The maximum height of the equipment should not exceed fourteen feet (14'). The Committee may require written consent from adjacent neighbors before approving an equipment Design Review Request
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.EEE, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards let owners add exterior lights without approval when they match the builder's style, are as small as practicable, point toward the house and run at low wattage, while high-wattage spotlights or floodlights need committee approval.
quote: Committee approval is not required for exterior lighting which is in accordance with the following regulations: Exterior lights must be of the same style and character as those installed by builder on other Homes or Lots and be as small in size as is reasonably practicable. Exterior lighting should be directed towards the Owner's Home and must be of low wattage to minimize glare sources to neighbors. … Any variance from these Design Standards or use of high wattage spotlights or floodlights requires Committee approval.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.QQ, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards let owners install underground irrigation without committee approval but say it should not go within 5 feet of the foundation.
quote: IRRIGATION SYSTEMS - Underground manual or automatic irrigation systems will not require approval of the Committee. Such systems should not be installed within five feet (5') of the foundation.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.MM, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards ask for professionally prepared plans for major improvements such as room additions, decks or structural changes, and say simple drawings and descriptions may be sufficient for other improvements, whether the owner or a professional draws them.
quote: In the case of major Proposed Improvements, such as room additions, decks, or structural changes, detailed plans should be professionally prepared by an architect, engineer, and/or draftsman, however, simple drawings and descriptions may be sufficient for other Proposed Improvements.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section III.D, on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Read from CDFPS.GOV.xx.DesignGuidelinesUpdatedJune2022.pdf, re-downloaded 2026-09-26 (md5 7d128450…). The next sentence begins 'Whether done by the Owner or professionally, the following provisions should be followed'. Differs from Declaration 10.13 ('professionally done' landscaping plans).

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards send design review requests to the association's management company and let the Design Review Committee obtain input from the Board on any request.
quote: All Design Review Requests should be made to the Association's Management Company … The Committee may obtain input from the Board related to any Design Review Request.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section III.C, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards limit gravel, rock and soil piles in front yards, visible side yards or on driveways to 15 days, allow none on the street, bar delivery trucks from crossing the greenbelt, entry and median areas, and hold the owner responsible for damage to common elements caused by the owner or the owner's agent.
quote: Gravel, rock, and/or soil piles left in front or on visible side yards of parcels, or on the driveway shall be left no longer than a period of fifteen (15) days. Gravel, rock, and/or soil piles are not permitted on the street. … Delivery trucks are not allowed to cross the greenbelt, entry, or median areas (to avoid sprinkler and landscape damage). If this regulation is violated and damage to the Common Elements results, the Owner will be held financially responsible for repairing the damage caused by the Owner or the Owner's agent, guest, invitee, or tenant.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.PP.2 and II.PP.3, on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's Design Standards bar gates or removable sections in perimeter fences and any rear or side yard access through them, require committee approval for gates, and do not permit double gates or gates opening to the street or open space other than those the builder installed.
quote: Perimeter Fences may not have gates or removable sections of any sort. There can be no rear or side yard access through perimeter Fences. … Gates - Committee approval is required. Double gates are not permitted. Gates opening to the street (other than installed by builder) or open space are not permitted.
source_label: Falcon Point at Saddleback Homeowners Association, Design Standards (June 2022), Section II.DD.1 and II.DD.3(e), on the association's TownSq documents page

fact: Falcon Point's declaration says a Design Review Committee approval is not a precedent for any other matter and does not waive the committee's right to deny later requests.
quote: The approval or consent of the Design Review Committee, or any representative thereof, to any application for approval shall not be deemed to constitute a waiver of any right to withhold or deny approval or consent by the Design Review Committee or any representative thereof, as to any application or other matters whatsoever as to which approval or consent may subsequently or additionally be required. Nor shall any such approval or consent be deemed to constitute a precedent as to any other matter.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Falcon Point at Saddleback, Section 5.10 (recorded September 20, 2019), on the association's TownSq documents page
notes: Design Standards III.I.3 ('No Precedent') says the same.
